1.explanation:
• list.scss: This SCSS file ships the rule `.bx--list--ordered:not(.bx--list--nested) > .bx--list__item:before { counter-reset: item; ... }` which is the root cause of the Firefox numbering bug. It must be updated to conditionally remove or unset the counter-reset when the native style class is present.

• OrderedList.js: This React component defines the useNativeStyles flag and applies the bx--list--native class, but the underlying CSS does not respond to that class. The component and its className logic need to be coordinated with the updated SCSS so that bx--list--native correctly disables the counter rules.

• OrderedList-test.js: New or updated tests should verify that when useNativeStyles is true, the list renders with the native decimal style (i.e. no pseudo-counter content), and in particular that counter-reset is not applied.

• OrderedList-story.js: Storybook needs an example demonstrating the useNativeStyles prop and showing the difference between the default counter-based style and the native decimal style, so users can preview and select the correct behavior.

• OrderedList.mdx: Documentation should be updated to describe the useNativeStyles prop, its effect on switching to native browser decimals (and disabling the counter-reset CSS), and the reason for doing so (Firefox bug). This ensures that consumers know about the workaround and can adopt it.
1.bug_scenario: In Firefox the Carbon ordered-list styling (using CSS counters and a ::before pseudo-element driven by counter-reset: item) doesn’t reset properly, so list numbering starts at a seemingly random offset (e.g. 7,8,9… instead of 1,2,3…). Attempts to override counter-reset in application CSS fail due to the built-in specificity of Carbon’s counter-based rules. The only thing that works is removing the counter-reset entirely from the shipped SCSS. The desired behavior is to allow a “native” ordered list style (decimal) when the React prop useNativeStyles (which adds the bx--list--native class) is true, so that lists in Firefox fall back to the browser’s built-in numbering and render correctly.

2.bug_scenario: When you render a Carbon OrderedList in Firefox that uses the default CSS-counter implementation (the pseudo-element + counter-reset approach), the list numbers start at seemingly “random” offsets (7, 8, 9, …). That is because Carbon’s SCSS for `.bx--list--ordered:not(.bx--list--nested)` always does `counter-reset: item`, and Firefox doesn’t reset it back to 1 in nested contexts the way WebKit-based browsers do. Attempts to override it with inline styles (`counter-reset: none` or `counter-reset: unset`) have no effect because Carbon’s stylesheet rule has equal specificity and later loading order. The only way to fix it today is to remove the `counter-reset: item` rule entirely, but that breaks the built-in pseudo-number styling. The intended workaround—using the `useNativeStyles` prop on `<OrderedList useNativeStyles>`—adds a `bx--list--native` class but there is no matching CSS to disable the custom counter, so it still fails in Firefox.
